name: Mammalian Pol II transcription of a polyadenylated protein-coding RNA
scope: A teaching synthesis. Human promoter complexes (5IY6/5IY8), a bovine polymerase on a synthetic elongation scaffold (5FLM), and mammalian biochemical/cellular evidence are separate sources. The gene length, elapsed time, RNA path and stage overlap are schematic.

closed.use: Human closed holo-PIC. All modeled polymer chains and deposited Mg/Zn retained in source coordinates.

initial.use: Human initially transcribing holo-PIC. Its X/Y polymer coordinates are both DNA. The six-position teaching RNA guide is fitted from 5FLM, not deposited RNA.

elongation.use: Bovine Pol II, synthetic nucleic acid scaffold. Chain P residues 15–20 supply a backbone guide, without transferring nucleotide identities to the distinct human promoter.

cleavage.use: Human CPSF73 catalytic segment, with all four modeled Zn positions and the crystallization sulfate. Shown alongside the cleavage site as a scale-adjusted enzymatic landmark, not a complete active processing complex.

promoter.supports: Human PIC closed, open and initial transcribing states. The sequence of prepared specimens does not supply an interpolatable trajectory.

opening.supports: XPB/TFIIH ATP-dependent promoter opening and roles in efficient promoter escape.

elongation.supports: Deposited mammalian elongation scaffold. Local C then U additions and two PPi fates reuse the editable teaching reconstruction.

processing.supports: PAS-dependent mammalian pre-mRNA cleavage and polyadenylation. CPSF73 acts within the processing machinery. Poly(A) polymerase extends the upstream 3′ end using ATP; cleavage itself is not depicted as ATP hydrolysis.

torpedo.supports: CPSF73-mediated cleavage gives the polymerase-associated downstream RNA a new 5′ end. XRN2 degrades it 5′ to 3′ and promotes efficient termination.

release.supports: PAS-dependent pausing and allosteric effects cooperate with XRN2. The visual separation from DNA is illustrative; the approach of a marker is not a measured ejection mechanism.

reuse.supports: Human FCP1 can dephosphorylate Pol II and regenerate initiation-competent polymerase. Order shown for clarity; the phosphatase can also act on elongation complexes.

energy_and_fates: XPB uses ATP during the selected opening route. NTP incorporation releases PPi in the two explicit elongation cycles.

Following cleavage, ATP supplies AMP for the upstream poly(A) tail. The downstream fragment is degraded from its exposed 5′ end; loss of RNA contour represents degradation products returned to the nucleotide pool.

CTD phosphate symbols represent reversible phosphorylation, not the number, sites or order of all CTD modifications. Released polymerase returns to the initiation-competent pool. RNA maturation/export downstream of polyadenylation is outside this route.

visual_identity.coding_rna: Coral upstream RNA body, local 3′ end and mature-side cleavage product
visual_identity.xrn2: Mint-rimmed activity marker for XRN2, not a molecular surface

omissions: The full gene, promoter-specific activators, enhancer control, cap, splicing, mRNA export and the full repertoire of alternative termination pathways are outside this basal coding-gene route. The RNA is a shared teaching identity across separate experimental constructs; intact native meshes are retained.
